about: Bits of freedom are what is left to decide in a cell: log2 of the states between the floor it requires and the ceiling it permits — the states in the upset of the floor that are also in the downset of the ceiling. A decided cell has none, and a cell in conflict has none either: no state satisfies it.
Resolution is chain length: on a chain the states between are an interval of it; on any lattice they are the interval [floor, ceiling] of its order.
